text: RR:190 combat-core blocker (1) calls the per-stance reach cap in stage px 'the one value the whole model needs' and prescribes measuring blade-FX tip-to-body span from footage. It does not need measuring. §1t1523s0§.as:2334-2348 computes it: §1t9592s0§() takes the SPD stat plus its bonus, multiplies by 1.5 under a speed buff, and returns §1t9593s0§(that), where §1t9593s0§(p) is 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));'. The un-obfuscated Android twin names every term - StatsManager.as:1915-1919 'internal static function getBaseSlashLengthVal(speed:int) : int { var maxincrement:int = 90 + getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(maxincrement * speed / (20 + speed))); }'. So BASE_SLASH_LENGTH = 120 + floor((90 + DAN*5) * SPD / (20 + SPD)), a saturating curve: SPD 0 -> 120, SPD 20 -> 165, SPD -> large -> 210 at DAN 0. Reach then = base x stance, per §1t99s0§.as:3094/:3105/:3116-3120 - Light x1.4 flat, Balanced x(1 + 0.02m), Heavy x(0.5 + 0.04m) floored at 100 absolute units. THIS ALSO SETTLES THE 300/200/100 TRIPLE: at a high-SPD, DAN-0 base of ~210 the MASTERY-0 row is 294 / 210 / 105, which is the ledger's 300/200/100. The triple is a mastery-ZERO row at high SPD, not a mastery-ceiling row - the ceiling multipliers are 1.4 / 1.2 / 0.9, which cannot make 3:2:1 off any single base. That independently confirms the arithmetic objection inside claim combat-core/stance-reach-is-asymmetric (whose OTHER objection, about RR:156's low endpoint, I refuted).

text: The forge finding in this packet says it 'pairs with the reinforce finding already in this packet'. There is no reinforce finding in this packet, so I went and read it. The result is a HALF-correction to the same ledger line, and it is different in shape from the forge one, which is why it must not be assumed. The COIN cost genuinely IS a static — InteractUI.as:1083 'cost = 5000;' with no formula, and all three display strings hard-code 'Cost: 5000 coins'. The MATERIAL is not: it branches on the equipped WEAPON's level, not the node level, at :1097-1131 — below 30 costs 1x 20064, below 60 costs 1x 20065, otherwise 1x 20066, with a special case at :1098-1101 forcing itemID 13022 to weaponlevel 59. I resolved the ids: 20064 Silver Ore, 20065 Titanium Ore, 20066 Uncut Diamond, matching strings.json["850"]/["851"]/["852"] exactly. The effect is settled at :1133 'weapon.uses = 0;' — unbreakable, which is what the copy promises. So RR:80's 'Reinforce 5000c+1 silver ore' carries the lowest of three material tiers and presents it as the whole rule, the same defect the forge finding identifies, but the price half of RR:80 survives here where it did not for forge. PARITY CAVEAT, stated because it is undischarged: I could not confirm the 5000 on the web side, so this row is v0.682 under S0-3.
